learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with a global and integrated understanding of the structure, organization, and function of the cell, and how this understanding is achieved.
Discuss the basic principles of the chemical and biological structure, organization, and function of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, with a special emphasis on mammalian cells.
The student has acquired sufficient basic knowledge in cell biology to easily follow the subsequent courses: Cellular Biophysics, Tissue Mechanics, and Modeling of Tissue Physiology.
The student has sufficient insight into the basic processes characteristic of living matter (reproduction, metabolism, differentiation, evolution).
The student has sufficient basic knowledge of genetics, biochemistry, cell biology, and cell physiology and masters the essential vocabulary of cell biology.
The student has sufficient insight into a limited number of techniques used to study cell biology.

syllabus_topics: Chemical and molecular fundamentals of cell biology: The cell = the basic unit of life
Chemical basic components of the cell
Organic reactions
Protein structure and function
Basis of molecular genetic mechanisms
Organization of cells: Biological membranes and the architecture of the prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell
Integration of cells into tissues
Principles of transport of ions and small molecules through cell membranes
Principles of energy metabolism in the cell
Genetic information and molecular biology: Molecular structure of genes and chromosomes
Transcriptional control of gene expression (transcription factors, microRNAs)
Principles of post-translational control of gene expression
Signal transduction in the cell: Signal transduction at the cell surface
Signal transduction in the control of gene activity
Nuclear transport and membrane transport: Nuclear transport
Overview of protein sorting and transport in eukaryotic cells
Molecular mechanisms of vesicular transport
Mitosis: Overview of cell division (mitosis) and control mechanisms
Meiosis: a special form of cell division
Cell differentiation: Stem cells
Specification and differentiation of cells
Cancer cells
Methods in cell biology: Derivatives of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR)
Antibody-based methods

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (multiple-choice questions with guessing correction, short knowledge questions, longer insight questions, application question)

assessment_rules: The exam includes multiple-choice questions (graded with guessing correction), shorter questions assessing specific knowledge, longer questions assessing insight, and a question requiring the analysis of a relatively simple scientific application of the course material. The modality of the second examination opportunity is the same as that of the first examination opportunity.
